successors.name: Second Polish Republic
successors.text: most of pre-war West Prussia (62%, with Danzig), without the eastern territory round Marienwerder, Stuhm, Marienburg and Elbing and the western remainder round Deutsch Krone and Flatow

ledger.x: 1773: 'West Prussia was established as a province of the Kingdom of Prussia in 1773'; 'The Partition Sejm ratified the cession on 30 September 1773'.
1775: 'from 1775 onwards the Netze District was administered with West Prussia'.

1793: 'Further Polish areas were annexed in the Second Partition of Poland in 1793'; this added Danzig and Thorn (Province page); the Second Partition page lists 'the cities of Gdańsk (Danzig) and Toruń (Thorn)' in Prussia's 58,000 km2.
1807: 'it also lost Danzig, which was a Free City from 1807 until 1814'.
1806-1807: 'West Prussia lost its southern territory in the vicinity of Thorn and Kulm' to the Duchy of Warsaw (Treaties of Tilsit).

9 July 1807, Treaties of Tilsit: 'large parts of the southern district went to the Bydgoszcz Department of the Duchy of Warsaw'; the north-western part round Wałcz and Kamień 'was incorporated into West Prussia' (the Province page says the Netze areas were 'added to West Prussia' in 1815 and 'The remainder became part…
1815: 'After the final defeat of Napoleon in 1815, Danzig, Kulm, and Thorn were returned to West Prussia'.
1815: Kulm and Thorn return from the Duchy of Warsaw's former land.
1829: West Prussia and East Prussia are 'officially combined by a cabinet order to form the Province of Prussia' (in personal union under a single Oberpräsident since 1824); it lasted until 1878.
1878: 'They were re-established as separate provinces in 1878.'

1919: 'After the Treaty of Versailles in 1919, most of pre-war West Prussia's territory (62%)' went to Poland or the Free City of Danzig; 'West Prussia was dissolved in 1919' (lead; the body also says 1920).
1919: Danzig leaves the province for the Free City of Danzig (Treaty of Versailles).

1919: West Prussia is dissolved; successors are Posen-West Prussia and the Region of West Prussia (infobox); the lead gives 1919, the body 1920, and 'the western remainder formed Grenzmark Posen-West Prussia in 1922'.

wars.name: First Partition of Poland
wars.outcome: Prussia took 36,000 km2 and about 600,000 people: most of Royal Prussia, Warmia, the Netze District and northern Kuyavia, not Danzig or Thorn; West Prussia formed in 1773 (the Netze District joined it in 1775).

wars.name: Second Partition of Poland
wars.outcome: Prussia took 58,000 km2 including Danzig and Thorn, which went to West Prussia; the rest was organised as South Prussia.
